thread.title: Apple Reports Earnings Today. Here's What to Expect.

title: Apple Reports Earnings Today. Here's What to Expect.
text:
Apple Reports Earnings Tomorrow. Here’s What to Expect. By Updated Jan. 28, 2019 4:20 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by Nicolas Asfouri/AFP/Getty Images Text size
Tech giant Apple is scheduled to report fiscal-first-quarter (ended Dec. 29) financial results after the market closes on Tuesday.
Apple stock (AAPL) is down a bit less than 1% in January through Monday’s close at around $156 per share, compared to a rise of more than 6% for the S&P 500 .
Here’s a snapshot of Wall Street’s expectations and some recent history.
• Wall Street is looking for quarterly earnings of $4.17 per share using standard accounting methods, or $4.20 without them, on revenue of about $84 billion, according to FactSet. The consensus non-GAAP estimate recently moved down by a penny per share.
• On Jan. 2, the company guided investors toward $84 billion in revenue. While its statement didn’t specify an EPS number, it did include estimates of gross margin and operating expenses, a tax rate, and a sharecount.
• In the year-ago quarter, the company reported EPS of $2.07 using both standard and nonstandard accounting, on revenue of $88.3 billion. Newsletter Sign-up
• The company has said that the quarter will be the first in which it stops reporting unit sales for the iPhone, iPad, and Mac, a decision some investors criticized.
• A conference call is scheduled for 5 p.m. E.T. on Tuesday.
This story was first published on Jan. 27, 2019. It was republished to reflect share price movement and to note the change in the consensus GAAP EPS estimate.
